answer.original_source: SemiAnalysis (report dated 2026-07-06, relayed by The Decoder, datacenterdynamics.com and others)
answer.new_information: SemiAnalysis adds that Nvidia scrapped the NVL72x2 fallback (two Oberon racks back to back) after cloud and hyperscale customers objected, and that the four-die Rubin Ultra version was canceled, leaving a two-die version with roughly half the real-world compute. It also says CPO-NVSwitch will not arrive until Feynman. The NVL72x2 scrapping is the same claim as e101, so it adds no independent confirmation. The Rubin Ultra four-die cancellation is not in the stored pieces (e70 and e71 cover only a rack slip and a PCB midplane problem). All of it comes from one SemiAnalysis report, and the Nvidia reply is a generic 'roadmap is intact'.

arguments.statement: Lean: Kyber NVL144 is not launched by 2027-12-31. SemiAnalysis, relayed by CNBC and datacenterdynamics, reports the rack delayed to 2028 because the PCB midplane is hard to manufacture without defects (e64, e66, e98, e100, e101, e70, e71), and the 2026-07-06 record adds that the NVL72x2 fallback was scrapped and the four-die Rubin Ultra canceled, which removes a stopgap path. Nvidia's 'roadmap is intact' statements (e65, e72, e102) are nonspecific and do not give a Kyber date.
limitations: Single-source SemiAnalysis report, relayed by several outlets; not an independent confirmation
Rumour-tier; no Nvidia filing or shipment confirmation
Nvidia's denial is generic and gives no alternative date
The 2028 date is a report, not a launch
what_would_change_it: Nvidia announcement or shipment of Kyber NVL144 before 2027-12-31
Nvidia giving a specific Kyber date that falls inside 2027
Independent confirmation of the midplane fix or a revised roadmap

arguments.statement: Unresolved, leaning toward Kyber launching by 2028-12-31 but with real execution risk. The reported delay to 'more than 12 months, to 2028' (e98, e101, e64, e66) puts the target inside 2028, but the report gives no month. The scrapped NVL72x2 fallback and the four-die Rubin Ultra cancellation (incoming record, consistent with e101) leave no interim path if the midplane problem persists. Nvidia's 'roadmap is intact' (e65, e72, e102) opposes the delay but gives no date.
limitations: Single-source SemiAnalysis report, relayed; not independently confirmed
'2028' carries no month, so it may fall late in the year or slip past 2028
Rumour-tier; no shipment or filing evidence
what_would_change_it: Nvidia launch or shipment announcement of Kyber in 2028
A dated Nvidia roadmap update placing Kyber in or after 2029
Independent manufacturing or supplier confirmation of the PCB midplane yield issue or its resolution

answer.reason: The incoming record's core claim (NVL72x2 scrapped) is the same claim as e101 from the same SemiAnalysis report, so it is not independent. It moves the Kyber questions by removing a fallback path and adding the Rubin Ultra four-die cancellation, which is new relative to the stored pieces. The record does not bear on the other questions: it concerns rack design, not guarantees, revenue, capex, shipments or China.
